### Key takeaways

- Add velocity through the lower half: drive, stride and hip rotation

- **90/90 hip switch: Fail: difficulty or pain rotating.** Training: Hip mobility training.

## Pitching program
4-week off-season block, 3 pitching days per week. Pitch counts are ranges for the whole session including warm-up pitches.

### Week 1: Settle in: moderate volume, sharp mechanics
- **Day 1, Drill work (17-24 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (27-37 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Drop ball, Changeup.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (20-27 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Week 2: Build: a little more volume and intent

## Weight room program
**Main program: Foundational strength and control.** Build the base: single-leg control, hinge and squat patterns, trunk stiffness and shoulder durability before chasing power.
- Movement screen, box jump: generalized strength weaknesses, so Foundational strength first.
- Movement screen (hip lift-off or pure torque rotation): rotational training, so Rotational power added.
- Arm care is part of every pitcher's week.
- Movement screen (hip, shoulder or squat mobility): Mobility circuit added.

### From the movement screen
Training the coach's protocol prescribes for this athlete's results:
- Big toe and intrinsic foot muscle work
- Hip mobility training
- Anterior core exercises and rotational training
- Hip mobility training and quad stretching

### Foundation: Day A (Lower body and anti-rotation)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15.
- Goblet box squat: 3 x 8 at RPE 6-7 (Knees track over toes, sit back to the box)
- Split squat (bodyweight or light dumbbells): 3 x 8 each at RPE 6-7 (Front knee stays stacked, no inward collapse)
- Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 3 x 10 at RPE 6-7
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each side (Ribs down, resist the rotation)
- Side plank: 2 x 20-30 s each

### Foundation: Day B (Upper body pull, single-leg balance, arm care)
Warm-up: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10.
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift (reach): 3 x 8 each at RPE 6 (Slow, hips square)
- Half-kneeling one-arm dumbbell row: 3 x 10 each at RPE 7
- Push-up (incline if needed): 3 x 8-12 at RPE 7
- Lateral band walk: 2 x 12 steps each way
- Prone Y and T raise: 2 x 10 each
- Dead bug: 3 x 8 each side

Progression: Week to week add 1-2 reps per set until the top of the range, then add load and drop back to the bottom of the range. Every fourth week, cut sets by a third.

### Rotational power: Day A (Rotational power)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15, then 2 x 5 med ball scoop tosses (light).
- Medicine ball scoop toss (2-3 kg): 4 x 4 each side (Hips lead, arms follow)
- Medicine ball step-behind rotational throw: 3 x 4 each side
- Landmine rotation: 3 x 6 each side at RPE 7
- Goblet squat: 3 x 8 at RPE 7
- Half-kneeling cable chop: 3 x 8 each side

### Rotational power: Day B (Trunk stiffness and upper back)
Warm-up: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10.
- Anti-rotation split-stance cable press: 3 x 8 each side
- Chest-supported dumbbell row: 3 x 10 at RPE 7
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 each at RPE 7
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 25 m each hand
- Side plank with top-leg raise: 2 x 8 each side

Progression: Med ball work stays light and fast; progress by intent and distance, not ball weight. Add strength-lift load 2.5-5% when all reps feel RPE 7 or easier. Deload every fourth week.

### Add-on: Arm care and scapular durability
Arm care (10-15 min, most days).
- Band external rotation at 0° and 90°: 2 x 15 each
- Prone Y-T-W: 2 x 8 each
- Serratus wall slide with lift-off: 2 x 10
- Half-kneeling band row to external rotation: 2 x 10 each
- Eccentric biceps curl (light, slow 4 s lower): 2 x 8 each
- Sleeper or cross-body stretch (only if cleared by the clinician): 2 x 30 s

### Add-on: Hip and thoracic mobility
Mobility circuit (15 min, 3-4 x per week).
- 90/90 hip switch with lift-off: 2 x 6 each side
- Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch with reach: 2 x 30 s each
- Quadruped hip rotation (CARs): 2 x 5 each direction
- Open-book thoracic rotation: 2 x 8 each side
- Quadruped thread-the-needle: 2 x 8 each side
- Deep goblet squat hold with pry: 2 x 30 s

### Weekly schedule
- **Week 1** (RPE at the low end of each range): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 2** (Progress per the program's rule): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 3** (Progress per the program's rule): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 4** (Deload: cut sets by a third, keep technique crisp): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B

### Cautions
- Move to Lower-half power only once single-leg squats hold alignment for all reps.
- Stop rotational throws with any low-back pain; replace with anti-rotation holds.
- Any shoulder or elbow pain during arm care: stop and tell the coach.
- Internal-rotation deficits are flagged for the clinician; the stretch is included only with their okay.
- Mobility work should never be painful; stop and tell the coach if it is.
